newsitem.title: USA: Northeast Utilities names new training head.
newsitem.headline: Northeast Utilities names new training head.

text.p: Northeast Nuclear Energy Co said Tuesday it had appointed Richard Johannes as director, nuclear training in its nuclear training department.
Johannes will replace Harry Haynes, who had been transferred.
Johannes worked at the Wolf Creek Nuclear Power Station, it said, adding that he was recently on loan to the Nuclear Energy Institute as director of finance and administration.
Moody's Investors Service Inc has downgraded Northeast, while other credit rating agencies are thinking about doing the same amid growing regulatory and financial uncertainties.
The uncertainties come from the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission's Feb 28 decision about interim stranded cost recovery for the state's largest electric utility.
The company filed a suit against the commission, challenging the restructuring order.
Northeast is also facing problems over proposed deregulation in the state and persistent woes related to the shutdown of its three Millstone nuclear plants in Waterford, Connecticut since March 1996.
One credit rating agency estimated the shutdown problems had already cost the company nearly $600 million.
Northeast nevertheless plans to renew operations at the plants by early 1998.
